items.summary: Legal disposition: conditional for ordinary reversible growth; blocked for new public exposure, security-sensitive releases, and SearchWoot public beta. Evidence: compliance baseline is 35 pass, 20 fail, and 6 unknown across 61 checked sites, with open banner, consent accept/reject, GA4, privacy, and terms findings; security controls and operations sweeps remain unevidenced; revenue includes $4.92 aggregate unattributed commission only. Permit growth only where existing consent, disclosures, provenance, claims, copyright/trademark, platform-policy, and age-sensitive boundaries are preserved. Keep SearchWoot private, preview-only, and unlaunched. Human counsel is required for Woot rights, privacy/jurisdiction, and future affiliate or advertising use.

Launch-readiness tracking remains active with four open legal tasks and no evidenced closures. Next evidence action: produce the read-only SearchWoot data-flow and retention table from repository and deployed configuration, covering alert rules, identifiers, sync results, Slack/email delivery, retention, deletion, correction, access, and unsubscribe behavior. Do not enable tracking, expand notifications, or change the private gate.

Maintain the existing security gate. Fleet-doctor, deployment, uptime, and error sweeps have no results; authentication, secrets, isolation, release, dependency, monitoring, incident, and disclosure evidence remain unknown. Continue dated read-only evidence capture; do not clear public exposure or security-sensitive releases.

For private or parked properties, retain the concrete decision: keep them parked, private, preview-only, and unlaunched. Do not build, publish, deploy, alter DNS, configure analytics, monetize, spend, or add queue work until ownership, preview/build, compliance, security, measurement-boundary, rollback, and explicit blocker evidence is attached.
